claims.claim: Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus
claims.source_checked: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-2/ (via Firecrawl, HTTP 200, page modified 2026-09-28); https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-024-02389-3 (doi:10.1038/s41550-024-02389-3, full text via Firecrawl)
claims.note: NASA: 'Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune.' Jasinski abstract: 'This single in situ measurement'. Page is current as of 2026-09-28, so no later visitor.

claims.claim: and it arrived at an unusual time.
claims.note: Abstract: Voyager 2 'observed Uranus's magnetosphere in an anomalous, compressed state that we estimate to be present less than 5% of the time'; Conclusions: 'highly atypical and compressed state'. 'Unusual time' = arrived during unusual conditions; it does not overstate.

claims.claim: Hook as heard by a viewer who swipes at second two: no spacecraft other than Voyager 2 has been to Uranus, and its visit happened at an untypical moment
claims.note: Both parts are true on their own, without the rest of the script: NASA confirms the single visit, and the paper says the conditions at arrival occur <5% of the time. The hook names no false popular version and says nothing about the planet itself being a fluke.
NASA: 'Closest approach to Uranus took place at 17:59 UT Jan. 24, 1986'. Paper Fig. 1 caption: bow shock crossed 24 January 1986 at 07:28 UT.

claims.claim: In the days before, the solar wind had picked up and squeezed the magnetic bubble around the planet.
claims.note: Main: density and dynamic pressure 'steadily increasing for 2 days (including a modest increase in v) before the flyby, from ~0.005 nPa to 0.018 nPa'. Conclusions: 'The magnetosphere of Uranus was continuously compressed (from ~28 to ~17 R_U) for the days leading up to the Voyager 2 flyby.' Magnetic bubble = magnetosphere is a fair plain-English gloss. Caveat for visuals (A6): the pre-flyby standoff distances are estimates computed from the solar wind, not observations, and days 16-21 are a data gap.

claims.claim: Researchers estimate it is squeezed that hard only about four percent of the time.
claims.note: 'a Voyager 2-observed magnetopause R_SS of 17.3 R_U or lower is expected to occur only 4% of the time at Uranus'; abstract and Conclusions give '<5%'. 'Researchers estimate' keeps it an estimate, which is right: it rests on Voyager 2 solar-wind data from Oct 1985 to Jun 1986 (solar minimum).

claims.claim: Had Voyager arrived about a week earlier, the solar wind pushing on that bubble would have been about twenty times weaker.
claims.note: Main: 'eight days before the flyby started, P_dyn was even lower at 0.001 nPa, with a minimum at 0.00078 nPa on day 13. Such low-pressure values are ~18 to ~23 times lower than during the Uranus flyby itself' (0.018/0.001 = 18). Conclusions: 'Had Voyager 2 arrived at Uranus a week earlier ... the much weaker solar wind dynamic pressure at that time.' Abstract: '~20 times lower'. Eight days -> 'about a week' and 18x -> 'about twenty' is within A3 rounding. Correctly avoids the abstract's 'only a few days earlier' (2 days earlier was only ~4x lower). Note: exactly 7 days earlier (24 Jan minus 7 = day 17) falls in the day 16-21 data gap; the 18x value is from day 16.

claims.claim: So the extreme magnetic bubble we have described for forty years may just be what one unusual week looked like.
claims.source_checked: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-024-02389-3 (abstract; Effects on the Uranian magnetosphere; Conclusions)
claims.note: Abstract: 'the interpretation of Uranus's magnetosphere as being extreme may simply be a product of a flyby that occurred under extreme upstream solar wind conditions'; 'canonical extreme magnetosphere of the solar system'. Body: 'Compression-induced magnetotail activity for the week before the flyby'. The script keeps the paper's hedge ('may'). Forty years: Jan 1986 to Nov 2026 = 40.8 years. Scope: the paper's 'extreme' also covers the oblique, off-centre field, which the paper says its result is 'unlikely to change'; 'magnetic bubble' (defined in line 3 as around the planet) keeps it to the magnetosphere, so visuals must not show the field tilt, spin axis, rings or moons as the fluke (A6).
